notes:
Probed TC-54458 (fresh, __scratch__ 764138) as the primary subject, then TC-54455 (older, __readonly__ 764093, tags=[], steps=[]) as a second read to guard against a one-off; both returned 200 with an identically-shaped test_case object and no field-population differences attributable to age. No writes were made to either case (read-only). 

CHECK 1 (numeric id): NOT exposed as a real field on this read either - the nested schema explicitly documents 'no integer id in the body' and the guidance says the same, and the actual response for both cases confirms it: no id/numeric_id/test_case_id key anywhere in the body. The only way to recover the numeric id (1975349 for TC-54458, 1971631 for TC-54455) is parsing the trailing path segment of urls.self, exactly as with create. Unlike the create-time precedent (get_test_plan/create_test_plan pair) where the create contract wrongly claimed the id was absent when it was actually parseable, THIS contract is honest in both directions: it says there's no id field, and there is genuinely no better way to get it than URL-parsing. So the read contract's honesty here matches the good half of that precedent (the read side), not the bad half.

CHECK 2 (status/case_type): Both come back POPULATED on this v2 read - status: "Active", case_type: "Other" - for both TC-54458 and TC-54455. This confirms the create-probe's hypothesis: the earlier list_folder_test_cases_v1 read returning status: null, case_type: null for the same TC-54458 row is that v1 listing's own default column-selection behaviour, not a real data inconsistency. get_test_case_v2 (fetching one case in full) does not share that omission.

CHECK 3 (attachments): This read returns attachments as an explicit empty array ([]), not an omitted key, for both cases probed. That means the create response's behaviour - declaring attachments as an array type but omitting the key entirely when there are no attachments - is NOT a shared 'omit when empty' convention across this API. The get_test_case_v2 read is the more conventional one (present as [] when empty); the create_test_case_v2 response is the outlier that should be flagged for that endpoint specifically, not generalized as house style.

Contract self-consistency note (not a response drift): the flat `returns` array omits `folder_path`, while the nested per-field schema declares it (documented there as 'only present on list responses, not single-case responses'). The actual response for both probed cases has no folder_path key, which is exactly what the nested schema's own caveat predicts - so the flat array's omission happens to match observed behaviour here, but the flat/nested disagreement itself is worth recording per the standing lesson about the flat returns array being unreliable in both directions, even though it did not cause a real declared_missing in this case. Similarly, feature/background/scenario (Gherkin-only) and review_status/reviewers (Review & Approve-only) are declared in both the flat and nested schema but absent from both probed cases' responses - both cases use template test_case_steps (not test_case_bdd) and the project apparently does not have Review & Approve enabled, so per the contract's own explicit conditional guidance this absence is expected, not drift.

Every other field the nested schema declares (identifier, title, description, preconditions, template, folder_id, status, priority, case_type, automation_status, owner, tags, issues, steps, custom_fields, attachments, is_shared, created_at, created_by, last_updated_at, updated_by, urls.self) was returned with the declared type on at least one of the two probed cases, and no key came back that the nested schema does not mention. This is not a hollow contract - the schema declares ~20 substantive fields and all were checked against real, non-empty (where applicable) data. Verdict: PASS.
